My son just turned 14, and recently started showing extreme anger, rage, violence.

He has always been a great kid, lots of activities, pretty decent grades, gets along great with everyone, never had an unkind word to say about anyone.

His mother and I separated when he was 4, but have since become friends again, and we get along great now. We live about 15 minutes apart, and are both equally active in his life - school, sports, band, etc.

I remarried 3 years ago, and my son and my new wife get along fantastically - I made it a point to sit down with him and make certain he has no issues with her, and he seemed genuinely surprised that I even asked him.

About a month ago, I got a call from his school; he had said something to a friend of his that included the word 'suicide.' The school counselor followed the school's policy regarding such things, and had us take him to a nearby children's hospital where we were met by a social worker who spoke with him, with us, and with all of us together. She felt that there was no serious threat to his safety, but recommended he spend a week in a juvenile mental health and addiction center for observation. She said it's just policy.

After a week there, they sent him home with no serious issues found - he had just broken up with his first girlfriend, and they felt that he simply wasn't dealing with it very well. They recommended that he see a therapist every couple of weeks just to make sure everything is going well for him. He acted just fine; the staff at the center said he was a sweet kid, very kind and friendly and helpful (just like he always is.)

Everything seemed to be fine; we had the "breaking up is hard" talk, and he seemed to be ok, other than saying, with tears in his eyes, "I just really miss her." The word 'suicide' was just his friend trying to get him to see the school counselor; my son said he never actually said that himself, his friend was just worried that he was so sad after the breakup.

Last weekend, we wanted to wrap up moving into our new house by taking the last 3-4 loads of stuff from the old house (last of the clothes, some stuff in the garage, lawn ornaments, etc.) Less than 5 minutes after we got to the old house, I handed him a pile of stuff to take out to the truck, told him to only take what he could carry, and he announced in a completely out-of-character rant, "God you are such an asshole!"

I should point out that none of us has ever heard a negative word come out of his mouth toward or about anyone at all, certainly never any name-calling. We've only ever seen him in a confrontation once, at one of his little league games one of the opposing team's players tried to start some shit after being struck out, my son simply walked away from him. He's truly not a fighter.

The conversation went like this:

What did you just say?

You heard me, you're just a fucking asshole. I'm calling mom to come get me and I'm NEVER FUCKING COMING BACK!!!

He went outside, and his mom called me a minute later; he told her that he just wanted to go to her house... in a completely calm voice and attitude. He said I yelled at him because he broke something and he just wanted to leave. (Nothing was broken, there was no yelling other than his. He said he didn't want to help us move, and wanted her to pick him up. She told him to see if he could just hang out at the new house until we got done; he has his Xbox and TV hooked up, she thought he could entertain himself until we got done (we only moved 6 blocks, so not like we were abandoning him. I said "That's fine, but he was really angry about something. I've never seen him act like that before."

She hadn't seen his outburst, and I don't think she fully believed it was as bad as I described - and she had no reason to, this was a new thing from him in every way.

I hung up, and told him I'd take him back to the other house.

"Fuck that, and fuck you! Just fucking leave me alone! I'm never fucking coming back here again!" (This was in the front yard, and he went on like this long and loud enough that most of the neighborhood was now looking to see the show.)

I told him to walk back to the new house and calm down and wait for us so we could talk about what's going on.

"Nothing's going on except you're just a fucking asshole!"

He took off down the street and banged on the front door of a house about 4 doors down; I do not know who lives there. He told the guy that answered "I'm scared of my dad and I need the police!" At that point, the guy took him inside and a few minutes later there were 3 cop cars there. They talked to me, talked to him, talked to the neighbors - all of whom said that this was definitely NOT normal, that I was always a good neighbor and never did anything that would cause his actions. The lady next door even came over and said what a sweet kind and gentle kid he has always been.

I told the officers about his stay at the mental health center, how we all thought everything was fine, about the breakup. They decided it would be best if he went to the hospital and have someone look him over, "just to be safe."

His mom and I got to the hospital at the same time, and the staff told us how wonderful he was, what a nice boy, he's so sweet.

They had him in the psych ward (I guess... ER entrance, multiple heavy steel locked doors and security cameras, everything behind safety glass, lots of people screaming and moaning in nearly every room.)

When we went in to see him, he was all smiles and sunshine. I started by asking him why he said I yelled at him for breaking something.

"I never FUCKING said that!"

His mom almost fell over at the reaction, and said "that's exactly what you told me. Why are you so angry? You're scaring me."

"I fucking hope you're scared!" And he punched the wall when he screamed that, his face crimson red.

We then met with the resident psychiatrist; he got all of our info about the past month, about the past 14 years, then went and met with our son for about an hour.

Then we all met.

From the psychiatrist: He's tired, exhausted, the old house was hot, the kids at school picked on him (he went from the mental health center straight to Spring break, hasn't been to school since the day they called me.)

Our son said "Well they are picking on me by texting me."

His mom said "hand over the phone."

The psychiatrist said he may be suffering from Oppositional Defiance Disorder, and suggested we discuss it with his therapist. He also recommended a 6-week program called a "Partial Hospitalization Program" - 10 hours a day every day in group sessions, one-on-one sessions, family sessions, custom treatment programs and so on, then evenings at home. After 6 weeks, an evaluation / review to see what steps come next, if any. He also suggested that "Since he's anxious that his room isn't fully unpacked yet, maybe it would be better if he stayed at his mom's tonight." Which is what happened.

Yesterday evening, my wife and I took him out to dinner, but he refused to talk about any of it, and it looked like he was starting to get mad about it so we backed off. Last night, his mom texted me and my wife with a quick review of what she found on his phone - hate-filled chats with a friend of his - extremely racist, bigoted, anti-gay, anti-semitic, anti-christian, misogynistic, vulgar descriptions of his ex girlfriend, and on and on. The back of his phone (inside the otterbox, on the phone itself) were swastikas, hand-written anti-everything messages, lots of troubling stuff. When asked about that, his answer was "Don't worry, it will wipe off, it isn't permanent marker."

In addition, no texts from anyone that looked like "picking on," but he did send a few messages from the hospital before we got there - "I'm not going through that fucking program again, I'll just talk my way out of it. Can you come over tonight and bring Crysis?" Along with that, a message (I assume from facebook, she didn't say) asking if you would kill a puppy for a million dollars - he texted one of his friends a very detailed, graphic description of exactly HOW he would kill a puppy... too disturbing to even repeat.

From what I saw, he didn't want to help move, so he did whatever it took to go back to his mom's and do whatever he wanted. And, in his eyes, it worked perfectly.

Today, we are waiting to hear from the therapist, from the mental health center, and I'm sure a few more places I can't think of at the moment.

I am afraid. That kind of instant rage makes me fear for his safety, and honestly the rest of the family as well - the look in his eyes when he had his outbursts makes me truly wonder if I want to fall asleep with him in the house.

It seems like he is very good at turning his "sweet boy" persona on and off as needed to get his way and to keep the mental health people satisfied that there isn't really anything seriously wrong. And it seems like he really doesn't care about anyone else or how his actions are affecting anyone else at all.

I just don't know what to do.
